steps.description: Fit DESeq2 on the raw counts with design ~ condition. Set the condition factor reference level explicitly to the control level as named in metadata.csv (do not rely on alphabetical ordering) and name the contrast as c('condition', <treated level>, <control level>) so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. Pre-filter minimally: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). Do NOT fit a batch term — the model matrix with condition and batch is rank-deficient because B1 holds every control and B2 every treated sample — and do NOT apply ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, limma removeBatchEffect, RUV or SVA, since removing the batch removes the condition. Run the Wald test, keep the DESeq2 count-outlier policy (with 6 replicates per cell, Cook's-distance outliers get NA p-values) and report how many genes are NA from the outlier flag separately from those removed by independent filtering. Plot the histogram of unadjusted p-values before adjustment and describe its shape. Adjust with Benjamini-Hochberg using independent filtering, passing alpha=0.05 to results() to match the reporting cutoff. Shrink log2 fold changes with apeglm on the condition coefficient for ranking and plotting, keeping the unshrunken estimate and lfcSE in the output table. Write the full results table for every tested gene (gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue, padj) — the Wald `stat` column is required downstream for enrichment. Every output file and figure must carry a header or caption stating that the condition effect is perfectly confounded with the processing batch.

steps.description: Take the complete DESeq2 results table from T1S2 — every tested gene, not a thresholded subset — and rank genes by the Wald `stat` column. The ranking-metric choice is disputed in the literature; this plan states its side: the Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its standard error and does not saturate into ties the way a signed p-value does. Map gene symbols to the identifier space of the gene set collection using the human organism annotation package, reporting the share of tested genes that failed to map and dropping many-to-many mappings with a stated count; if the collections are served in symbol space, keep symbols throughout and never mix identifier spaces. Run fgsea against the human MSigDB hallmark gene sets first, then against a human Reactome pathway collection as the second pass, restricting to sets with 15-500 members after intersection with the tested genes, with BH adjustment and a fixed random seed. Collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea collapsePathways or an overlap-based grouping) and report one representative per group with the full table kept as a supplement. Record the leading-edge genes of each significant set with their gene-level statistic. Report the number of genes with padj < 0.05 from T1S2; if that number is below about 50, do not run any over-representation test on the discrete list — the ranked method on the full list is the analysis. Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets, and a human curated pathway collection (Reactome) for the second pass; the environment also holds a human WikiPathways GMT in gene-symbol space, which is an acceptable substitute for the second pass if a Reactome collection is not resolvable — say which was used and its version. Every output carries the confounding label: an enriched set describes the treated/B2 versus control/B1 difference, not a demonstrated treatment response.

Gene set collection names and versions recorded, together with the unmapped-identifier share and the number of many-to-many drops
Size window 15-500 applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Hallmark results and second-collection (Reactome, or WikiPathways with the substitution stated) results exported with NES, pval, padj, size and leading edge
Redundant significant sets collapsed, one representative reported per group, full table kept as a supplement
Random seed set and recorded

steps.question: What can and cannot be concluded about treated versus control lung gene expression from a design in which every treated sample was processed in batch B2 and every control in batch B1?

grounding.reason: Report content follows R-0041/R-0085/R-0087 for the DE fit, R-0042 for the two-method overlap, R-0051/R-0055/R-0105 for the enrichment section and R-0086 for the reproducibility record; the confounded label required by R-0005@668f leads the report.

constraints: Do not describe any gene or pathway as a treatment effect without the confounding qualifier attached
Rank genes for tables and figures by the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change, not the unshrunken estimate
Report the intersection of DESeq2 and edgeR as the high-confidence set; list method-specific genes separately
Do not introduce any new statistical test in this step
steps.description: Assemble a single report. Open it with the design limitation, stated plainly and before any result: batch B1 contains all 6 controls and batch B2 all 6 treated samples, therefore the condition effect and the processing-batch effect are mathematically indistinguishable in this dataset; no correction method can separate them; the reported fold changes are treatment-plus-batch differences and are interpretable as treatment effects only under the untestable assumption that the two batches introduce no systematic difference. Then report: the method and every package version, the design formula and the named contrast (condition, treated numerator, control denominator), the thresholds (BH padj < 0.05), the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes per method, the MA plot and the dispersion plot from the DESeq2 fit, the p-value histogram with its shape described, and the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE — ranked by the shrunken value for tables and plots, never by the unshrunken value alone. Include the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S3 as the high-confidence set with per-method counts. Include the enrichment section from T2S1 with the collection name and version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the collapsed representative sets and the leading-edge genes of each significant set, plus the statement that enrichment results are method-dependent. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, random seeds, and the gene-set collection version. State as the recommendation that a design in which each batch holds both conditions is required before any of these genes can be attributed to the treatment.

Method, package versions, design formula, named contrast, thresholds, n tested and n DE per method all present
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram included with a description of each
Gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE; ranking and plots use the shrunken value
DESeq2/edgeR per-method counts and intersection reported; union not presented as the result
Enrichment section states collection and version, rank metric, universe, size window, and lists leading-edge genes per significant set
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seeds, package versions and collection version stored alongside the results
Explicit recommendation for a batch-balanced re-design

plan.title: Treated vs control lung RNA-seq, batch-confounded DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12000 x 12 raw salmon gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12 x 3 sample table (metadata.csv) carrying condition and batch: 6 treated and 6 control lung samples, human. The design is fatally limited in one specific way: batch B1 holds all 6 controls and batch B2 holds all 6 treated samples, so the processing batch is perfectly confounded with the condition. No statistical procedure can separate a treatment effect from a batch effect here — a design matrix with both terms is rank-deficient, and ComBat-seq / removeBatchEffect / SVA would strip the condition effect along with the batch. The plan therefore fits condition alone, and every result carries an explicit confounding label: the reported log2 fold changes are treatment-plus-batch differences, valid as a treatment estimate ONLY under the untestable assumption that B1 and B2 introduce no systematic difference.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC before any model: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes — each plot coloured by both condition and batch, which in this design produce identical colourings; that identity is itself the finding to display, plus any outlier or depth anomaly. T1S2 fits the DESeq2 negative-binomial model with ~ condition, control as the explicit reference level, contrast condition treated vs control, minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), Wald test, apeglm shrinkage for ranking and plots, BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, and a p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment. T1S3 repeats the test with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and the same design and reports the intersection as the high-confidence set — robustness across methods is the only kind of robustness this design permits, since it cannot be checked against batch. T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes (ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed choice is settled toward the Wald stat because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate into ties) into fgsea against human MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome, with a 15-500 size window and redundant sets collapsed. T1S4 assembles the report: methods, versions, design, thresholds, n tested, n DE, MA and dispersion plots, shrunken and unshrunken LFC with lfcSE, leading-edge genes per significant set, sessionInfo — and, at the top, the confounding statement that governs the interpretation of everything below it.

No batch-correction step is planned, by rule and by logic. Counts are not pre-normalized; normalization stays inside the model as median-of-ratios size factors. The honest deliverable is a ranked list of genes that differ between the B2/treated and B1/control groups, explicitly not attributable to treatment.

Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples

Confounded-design report: methods, versions, design, thresholds, MA and dispersion plots, p-value histogram, shrunken and unshrunken LFC, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, leading edge genes, sessionInfo

Run fgsea against the human MSigDB hallmark gene sets first, then against a human Reactome pathway collection as the second pass, restricting to sets with 15-500 members after intersection with the tested genes, with BH adjustment and a fixed random seed. Collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea collapsePathways or an overlap-based grouping) and report one representative per group with the full table kept as a supplement. Record the leading-edge genes of each significant set with their gene-level statistic. Report the number of genes with padj < 0.05 from T1S2; if that number is below about 50, do not run any over-representation test on the discrete list — the ranked method on the full list is the analysis. Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets, and a human curated pathway collection (Reactome) for the second pass; the environment also holds a human WikiPathways GMT in gene-symbol space, which is an acceptable substitute for the second pass if a Reactome collection is not resolvable — say which was used and its version. Every output carries the confounding label: an enriched set describes the treated/B2 versus control/B1 difference, not a demonstrated treatment response.

steps.name: Confounded-design report
steps.question: What can and cannot be concluded about treated versus control lung gene expression from a design in which every treated sample was processed in batch B2 and every control in batch B1?
steps.description: Assemble a single report. Open it with the design limitation, stated plainly and before any result: batch B1 contains all 6 controls and batch B2 all 6 treated samples, therefore the condition effect and the processing-batch effect are mathematically indistinguishable in this dataset; no correction method can separate them; the reported fold changes are treatment-plus-batch differences and are interpretable as treatment effects only under the untestable assumption that the two batches introduce no systematic difference. Then report: the method and every package version, the design formula and the named contrast (condition, treated numerator, control denominator), the thresholds (BH padj < 0.05), the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes per method, the MA plot and the dispersion plot from the DESeq2 fit, the p-value histogram with its shape described, and the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE — ranked by the shrunken value for tables and plots, never by the unshrunken value alone. Include the DESeq2/edgeR overlap from T1S3 as the high-confidence set with per-method counts. Include the enrichment section from T2S1 with the collection name and version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the collapsed representative sets and the leading-edge genes of each significant set, plus the statement that enrichment results are method-dependent. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, random seeds, and the gene-set collection version. State as the recommendation that a design in which each batch holds both conditions is required before any of these genes can be attributed to the treatment.
steps.context: Final synthesis across T1S2 (DESeq2), T1S3 (edgeR cross-check) and T2S1 (enrichment) for the 12-sample human lung dataset.
